For a group G let Dn(G)=G∩(1+Δ(G)n) be its integral dimension subgroups and γn(G) its lower central series. Whether D5(G)⊆γ4(G) for every group is open (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 20.84). For Lie rings the analogous inclusion was recently proved by Ionin, Mikhailov and Petrov, and formally verified in Lean. This note collects what is known, records an elementary reduction of the group question to finite metabelian 2-groups of class three, analyses which steps of the Lie-ring proof have no group-theoretic counterpart, and reports computational evidence. For 3-torsion in D5/γ5 we prove D5(G)=γ5(G) whenever G/γ2(G) is finite and has at most one invariant larger than 3, and, with a computer search, for all 3-groups of order at most 39. We do not solve the problem.
